title: WebSocket Setup
description: Configure WebSocket connections for Apollo Client subscriptions using WebSocketLink and graphql-ws.

data.text: Apollo Client uses a **link-based architecture** to route operations to different transport layers. Queries and mutations travel over HTTP, while subscriptions need a persistent WebSocket connection. Setting up this connection correctly is critical for reliable real-time features.

Apollo Client provides `WebSocketLink` from `@apollo/client/link/ws` to handle WebSocket connections. For newer Apollo Client versions, the community-standard `graphql-ws` library is recommended because it offers better TypeScript support, connection lifecycle management, and reconnection strategies.

data.title: Classic WebSocketLink Setup

data.text: The `split` function routes operations to different links based on a test function. For subscriptions, we inspect the operation definition and check if it is a subscription operation. All other operations continue through the HTTP link.

data.title: Order Matters
data.text: Always place the WebSocket link as the first argument to `split`. If you place it second, queries might accidentally match a broader test and route to the wrong transport.

data.title: graphql-ws with Apollo Client 3.8+

data.text: WebSocket connections can drop due to network issues, server restarts, or mobile app backgrounding. Both `WebSocketLink` and `graphql-ws` support automatic reconnection, but their configuration differs. The `graphql-ws` library uses a `shouldRetry` callback for fine-grained control.

data.title: Custom Retry Logic with graphql-ws
Connection State Management
data.text: Relying solely on automatic reconnection can hide connection issues. Track the connection state and surface connectivity status to users so they know when real-time features are unavailable.

data.caption: WebSocket connection establishment and reconnection flow
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Start] --> B{WebSocket exists?}
    B -->|No| C[Create new connection]
    B -->|Yes| D{Is connected?}
    D -->|No| E[Wait for reconnect]
    D -->|Yes| F[Send subscription]
    C --> G[Init handshake + auth]
    G --> H{Server accepts?}
    H -->|No| I[Close and report error]
    H -->|Yes| J[Connection established]
    J --> F
    E --> F
    I --> K[End]
    F --> L[Receive updates]
    L --> M{Connection lost?}
    M -->|No| L
    M -->|Yes| E

data.content: Passing auth tokens on WebSocket connection

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use split to route subscriptions to WebSocket and queries/mutations to HTTP
graphql-ws is the modern standard over legacy WebSocketLink
connectionParams send auth tokens during the WebSocket handshake
Automatic reconnection handles network drops, but monitor connection state
data.takeaway: A correctly configured WebSocket link is the foundation of all real-time features.
